summary: The machine booted by UEFI firmware, OVMF, from its installed GPT disk, that disk's recovery entry, the disk with its menu deleted, the install stick and the recovery CD, each reached over SSH; the disk's BIOS core replaced and booted by either firmware; an install onto a 4 TiB NVMe disk whose root grows past 2 TiB, booted again and by its kernel given to QEMU; and a damaged primary GUID table written again from recovery; the program is tests/cases/machine/uefi_scenario.c

cases.behavior: OVMF boots the installed GPT disk from its EFI system partition; the kernel finds its root by the disk's GUID, makes the framebuffer write-combining and shows the login prompt on the framebuffer in its own font; root logs in over SSH and bootctl names the candidate as booted; Doom draws its picture on the framebuffer, and the console has the screen back once the game is killed

inputs.disk: the GPT disk mkdisk_grub.sh makes with the installer's ext2 root of 64 MiB, which stages the Doom WAD

execution.cleanup: libetude-case ends the machine and the game's ssh and removes the copy of the disk, which it keeps after a failure; the scenario removes its copy of the demo key and the screen dumps after a pass

steps.does: boot the disk by OVMF until init starts the SSH server and the server answers, and read the firmware's and the kernel's records, and the uid, bootctl status and the game's WAD over SSH
dump the screen through QMP and read the console's cells off the dump with screentext
run the game over SSH until it reports its first frame, count the screen's colors, stop the ssh, kill the game, wait until it has gone, count the colors again and end the machine with QMP's quit

services.does: run the game as root over SSH with its output on the connection, until the case stops the ssh

assertions.checks: the firmware's BdsDxe says on the serial line that it starts the boot option of the IDE disk, UEFI QEMU HARDDISK
the kernel names its root GPTID=GUID,3, /dev/disk0p3, ext2
the kernel reads the page attribute table back as 0x0007040600070106 and says the framebuffer is mapped write-combining
root logs in over SSH with the demonstration key, and id -u prints 0
bootctl status on the running machine says booted: candidate
the disk has /demo/doom1.wad, which its root stages from ports/doom/doom1.wad
a line of the framebuffer console's text, as screentext reads the dump against the kernel's font, begins rach2 login:
the game started over SSH reports its first frame drawn
the screen dumped once the game has reported its first frame has more than 64 colors, those of the game's palette
killall doom leaves no doom process
the screen dumped once the game has gone has at most the console's 16 colors

native.reason: the case reads which boot option the firmware started and dumps the screen through QMP, which only QEMU's firmware and monitor give

boot the copy by OVMF until init starts the SSH server and the server answers, read the command line and bootctl status of the boot partition over SSH, and end the machine with QMP's quit

the boot's /proc/cmdline has rach2.slot=recovery, and root's SSH login runs

cases.behavior: the installed GPT disk booted by SeaBIOS through its BIOS core: bootctl grub writes GRUB's GPT core into the BIOS boot partition's tail not in use and points the entry sector at it, leaving the table's sectors as they were; with the other tail zeroed on the host the disk boots by SeaBIOS through the new tail; a second install goes back to the first tail and is shown the same way; and the disk still boots by OVMF, whose path does not use the core

inputs.disk: the GPT disk of machine.uefi.installed, built with its core in tail A
inputs.core: vendor/grub/gpt-core.img, checked against the GRUB manifest

execution.cleanup: libetude-case ends the machine and removes the copy of the disk, which it keeps after a failure; the scenario removes its copy of the demo key after a pass

steps.does: read the BIOS boot partition and the entry sector's blocklist off the copy's GUID table, keep the table's sectors, and boot the copy by SeaBIOS until init starts the SSH server and the server answers
send the core over SSH and install it with bootctl grub, end the machine with QMP's quit, read the entry sector and the table's sectors, zero tail A, and boot by SeaBIOS until the server answers
install the core again, end the machine, read the entry sector and the table's sectors, zero tail B, boot by SeaBIOS until the server answers, and end the machine
boot the copy by OVMF until the login prompt and end the machine with QMP's quit

assertions.checks: the copy's GUID table has a BIOS boot partition, and its entry sector's blocklist names tail A, the sector after it
the first boot by SeaBIOS has no BdsDxe on its console, so no UEFI firmware made it
the kernel publishes the BIOS boot partition as /dev/grubcore: partition 4, of the table's sectors, at its first LBA
bootctl grub says it wrote the core in the tail at LBA B and that the entry sector at the partition's first LBA now points there
with the machine ended, the entry sector's blocklist names tail B
the protective MBR, the primary header and array and the backup array and header are the bytes they were before the install
with tail A zeroed, the disk boots by SeaBIOS until the SSH server answers
a second bootctl grub writes the core in the tail at LBA A and points the entry sector there
with the machine ended, the entry sector's blocklist names tail A
the table's sectors are still the bytes they were before the first install
with tail B zeroed, the disk boots by SeaBIOS until the SSH server answers
after both installs OVMF boots the disk to the login prompt, and its BdsDxe says it started the IDE disk's boot option

progress.means: a step of the manifest has ended

native.reason: bootctl grub writes GRUB's core into the BIOS boot partition of the booted disk, which on the Lenovo is the accepted system's boot loader, and the case zeroes the other tail from the host

cases.behavior: the install stick, booted by OVMF beside a sparse 4 TiB NVMe disk, installs onto that disk and grows its root into the whole of it; OVMF then boots the NVMe disk alone, the first account logs in with the key the install took and finds the root on the NVMe disk larger than 2 TiB; and the kernel given on QEMU's command line with rach2.root=ext2 finds that root, whose entry runs past 2 TiB, by its scan of the table's first four entries

inputs.answers: the NVMe disk, root's password twice, the account owner and its password twice, the demonstration key as its authorized key, no recovery key, the grow, and the disk again

execution.cleanup: libetude-case ends the machine and removes the copies of the stick and the sparse disk, which it keeps after a failure; the scenario removes its copy of the demo key and the answers after a pass

steps.does: boot the stick by OVMF beside the empty NVMe disk until the server answers, answer rach2-install over SSH, sync, and end the machine with QMP's quit
boot the NVMe disk alone by OVMF until init starts the SSH server and the server answers, read df of the root as the first account, and end the machine with QMP's quit
boot the kernel given to QEMU with rach2.root=ext2 and the NVMe disk until the kernel names its root, and end the machine with QMP's quit

assertions.checks: rach2-install, answered over SSH, says it grows the root into the rest of the disk and exits 0
the firmware's BdsDxe says on the serial line that it starts the NVMe disk's boot option
df -k / as the first account, logged in by the demonstration key, names /dev/diskNp3 with more than 2147483648 KiB
the kernel given to QEMU with rach2.root=ext2 says ext2: root: /dev/disk0p3

native.reason: the case installs onto and grows a 4 TiB disk, which only a sparse file under QEMU gives

cases.behavior: a GPT disk whose primary header does not check, beside the install stick booted by SeaBIOS: the recovery system names the disk as read from its backup table, diskctl relocate writes the primary again, whose header then checks, and the disk boots by SeaBIOS with its kernel reading the primary table

inputs.disk: the GPT disk of machine.uefi.installed with RACH over four bytes of its primary header's checksum

execution.cleanup: libetude-case ends the machine and removes the copies of the stick and the disk, which it keeps after a failure; the scenario removes its copy of the demo key after a pass

steps.does: write RACH over the primary header's checksum in the copy, boot the stick by SeaBIOS beside the disk until the server answers, run diskctl relocate /dev/disk0 and sync over SSH, end the machine with QMP's quit, and check the copy's primary header
boot the disk alone by SeaBIOS until the login prompt and end the machine with QMP's quit

assertions.checks: the recovery system's init says /dev/disk0: its primary GUID table does not check and was read from the backup
diskctl relocate /dev/disk0 says the primary table was written again from the backup
with the machine ended, the copy's primary header at LBA 1 has its signature and the CRC-32 of its bytes
the disk alone then boots by SeaBIOS through its BIOS core to the login prompt, and its kernel does not say the primary GPT is damaged, since GRUB boots a disk from its backup table as well
